cues.text: A typhoon is coming, and PAGASA draws its forecast track toward Albay.
cues.onscreen: Map of Bicol at sea level; a typhoon spiral moves in from the Pacific along a dotted forecast track with a widening cone; forecast points +12 h, +24 h, +36 h.

cues.text: Along the track, PAGASA raises wind signals, from Signal No. 1 up to Signal No. 5.
cues.onscreen: Signal rings 1 to 5 open around the forecast landfall; the ladder of the five Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals builds on the right (wind range per signal).

cues.text: Each signal comes with a lead time: thirty-six hours at Signal No. 1, but only twelve at Signal No. 4 or 5.
cues.onscreen: The lead-time column lights up: 36 h, 24 h, 18 h, 12 h, 12 h. Source: PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals (2022).

cues.text: Families must leave before the winds arrive. But where do they go, and is there room for Lola?
cues.onscreen: A family of four by their house; bubbles "Where do we go?" and "Room for Lola?".

cues.text: Albay has lived through this before.
cues.onscreen: Albay as a field of 720 barangay dots; Mayon at the centre. PSA 2020 census.

cues.text: In 2006, Typhoon Reming sent lahar down Mayon, and about 1,200 people were dead or missing.
cues.onscreen: Card: "November 2006 · Typhoon Reming (Durian) · lahar from Mayon's old deposits · about 1,200 dead and missing". Source: Philippine Daily Inquirer, 2016.

cues.text: In 2020, Super Typhoon Rolly made landfall in Albay under Signal No. 5.
cues.onscreen: Card: "November 2020 · Super Typhoon Rolly (Goni) · landfall in Tiwi, Albay · Signal No. 5". Source: PAGASA, 2020.

cues.text: And when Mayon rose to Alert Level 3 in January 2026, four schools became evacuation centers, and 3,424 learners were affected.
cues.onscreen: Card: "January 2026 · 4 schools became evacuation centers · 3,424 learners affected". Source: Philippine Daily Inquirer, 2026.

cues.text: The law makes schools a last resort. Goals 4, 11, and 13 meet in the same classroom.
cues.onscreen: Chips SDG 4.a, SDG 11.5 and SDG 13.1 meet over one classroom; "RA 10821: schools are evacuation centers only as a last resort".

cues.text: As the track shifts, the plan must shift too: which zones leave, and which roads close.
cues.onscreen: Badge "SIGNAL NO. 4"; a lead-time clock counts down from 12 h; test network E1 with its hazard zones.

cues.text: Heavy rain sends lahar down the river channels and closes the bridges.
cues.onscreen: Lahar channels A and B cut across the road ring; bridges A1 to A4 and B1 to B3 turn red with a cross.

cues.text: Send everyone to the nearest site, and families arrive at shelters that are already full.
cues.onscreen: Arrows to the nearest shelters; counter "898 arrive at full shelters" (test network E1, Alert Level 4 with typhoon lahar).

cues.text: So how do we shelter everyone before the lead time runs out, the vulnerable first, and classrooms last?
cues.onscreen: "Everyone sheltered · Vulnerable first · Classrooms last · Before the lead time ends" with a question mark.

cues.text: This is where MCS comes into play.
cues.onscreen: The letters M, C and S drop in and unfold into Mathematical, Computational, Sciences.

cues.text: Objective one: turn the signal and the forecast track into a hazard scenario, the zones that must leave and the roads that close.
cues.onscreen: Panel OBJECTIVE 1 · SCENARIO: σ = (Z_σ, X_σ); signal + track → zones (lahar, flood, storm surge) and closed roads; test network E1 with closed bridges.

cues.text: Objective two: write the law's order as one lexicographic minimum-cost flow: vulnerable first, everyone next, classrooms last.
cues.onscreen: Panel OBJECTIVE 2 · SHELTER PLAN: three shelter tiers, the lexicographic objective and its penalties; evacuee flows animate.

cues.text: Objective three: compute the exact clearance time on a time-expanded network, and check it against the signal's lead time.
cues.onscreen: Panel OBJECTIVE 3 · CLEARANCE TIME: T* = min{T : F(T) = D}; T* ≤ lead time; arrival curve F(T).

cues.text: Objective four: find the bridges to protect before landfall, and site new Ligtas Pinoy Centers with a proven guarantee.
cues.onscreen: Panel OBJECTIVE 4 · BRIDGES AND CENTERS: Δ_B = T*(σ + B) − T*(σ) ≥ 0; f(S_g) ≥ (1 − 1/e) f(S*); the new center lights up.

cues.text: Objective five: prove every result, then verify it against independent code.
cues.onscreen: Panel OBJECTIVE 5 · PROOF: ten proof marks turn into checks.

cues.text: On the test network, losing one lahar channel's bridges stretches the clearance time from 53 to 95 minutes.
cues.onscreen: Card 1: "Clearance time 53 → 95 min · lahar channel A closed · protect it first" (test network E1, synthetic).

cues.text: With typhoon rain on an eruption, 450 people are cut off, and one new center reaches 400 of them.
cues.onscreen: Card 2: "450 cut off → one new Ligtas Pinoy Center reaches 400".

cues.text: At Alert Level 3, the plan closes fourteen classrooms instead of forty.
cues.onscreen: Card 3: "Classrooms closed 40 → 14 · learners displaced 1,702 → 532".

cues.text: Ten results, proven, then verified against independent code.
cues.onscreen: Ten green checks; 300/300 plans, 660/660 networks, 4,796 checks, 0 violations.

cues.text: LIGTA-S will not stop a typhoon.
cues.onscreen: Boom. Screen darkens; the line appears in white.

cues.text: But before landfall, it will tell every family where to go, in time, and keep the most classrooms open.
cues.onscreen: The line appears in gold.

cues.text: A signal tells you the storm is coming.
cues.onscreen: "A signal tells you the storm is coming." in white.

cues.text: A plan tells you if there is room, in time.
cues.onscreen: "A plan tells you if there is room, in time." in gold.
